candidates.title: The concept graph's dry run prices its 92 requests as one prompt, so the recorded input and ceiling are five times what the build costs
candidates.area: literature_live graph --dry-run; the F.5 records (commit 0dd8415, docs/reports/literature-retrieval.md, docs/PROGRESS.md)
candidates.statement: literature_live.graph_command adds every batch's prompt characters into one count and prices that count with llm.cost_usd, so the Haiku 5.5 long-prompt tier (past 100,000 tokens) applies to all 92 batches, and the records' '0.2199 USD of input' and 'at most 2.3239 USD' stand where 92 requests at their own tier come to 0.0440 and 0.4648 USD.
candidates.contract: core/openferment_core/llm.py:340-345 'A model whose price rises with the prompt: past the threshold (in prompt tokens, cache reads and writes included) the whole request pays the second pair'; core/openferment_core/literature_live.py:11-13 'what their input and the most a build could cost come to on the route's first model (each batch's whole answer, the figure the day's cap holds against)'; the build sends one request a batch (literature/graph.py:15 'one model call on the client the caller hands in', graph.build:172), each held against the cap at its own size (llm.worst_case_usd:568-573). Recorded at docs/reports/literature-retrieval.md:115-117, docs/PROGRESS.md:609 and 3372, commit 0dd8415 ('at most 2.3239 USD on claude-haiku-5-5').
candidates.expected: The dry run prices each batch as the request it is (about 19,100 characters, 4,779 kit tokens, under the 100,000-token threshold): input 0.0440 USD, the most the 92 holds sum to 0.4648 USD.
candidates.observed: graph_command's own dry-run branch, fed 92 prompts summing to the recorded 1,758,899 characters, prints inputUsd 0.219862 and mostUsd 2.32393, the records' numbers to the digit: every token priced at the long tier (0.50 and 2.50 USD a million) where each request pays 0.10 and 0.50.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/literature_live.py:105-112 (chars = sum of every prompt; cost_usd(model, round(chars / 4), 0) and cost_usd(model, chars // 2 + len(prompts), answer * len(prompts)) price the sum as one request)
candidates.evidence: Ran bughunt/notes/R2/scripts/graph_dry_cost.py (stand-ins for the database read only; the code's own arithmetic): 'graph_command's dry run prints: ... "inputUsd": 0.219862, "mostUsd": 2.32393'; 'one request a batch: largest prompt 19119 characters, about 4779 kit tokens (the long-prompt threshold is 100000 tokens)'; 'input of the 92 requests at their own tier: 0.0440 USD (dry run says 0.2199)'; 'the most, each request's hold summed: 0.4648 USD (dry run says 2.3239)'. git grep shows 2.3239 and 0.2199 in docs/reports/literature-retrieval.md:116-117 and docs/PROGRESS.md:609, 3372.

candidates.title: conform against a database the server lacks runs every check and exits 0, where migrations refuse it in words with exit 2
candidates.statement: With OPENFERMENT_DATABASE_URL naming a database the PostgreSQL server does not hold, `conform biosteam` makes its checks, prints the driver's error and a sqlalche.me link for the verdict it could not keep, says 'every check holds' and exits 0, while `migrations migrate` refuses the same address in words with exit 2 and `conform train --project` exits 2 telling the person to start a server that is running.
candidates.contract: Commit 6f85338 (D.0): 'conform and migrations say a missing database in words (exit 2)'. docs/api/engines.md:805-807 'keeps its verdict in that address's database's engine_checks, with --project or without, once that database is migrated (pnpm db:migrate); a verdict it cannot keep is printed with the words why'.
candidates.reproCommand: bash bughunt/notes/R2/scripts/conform_missing_db.sh <a worktree of 2047f5a with its own core/.venv>
candidates.expected: conform refuses an address whose database is missing in words naming it and the command that makes it, exit 2, as migrations does ('the server at 127.0.0.1:5432 holds no database bh_r2_missing ...: pnpm db:reset <name> makes a database of that name there').
candidates.observed: migrations: 'refused: the server at 127.0.0.1:5432 holds no database bh_r2_missing ...' exit 2. conform biosteam: '! the verdict could not be kept for GET /api/engines: DBAPIError: (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.asyncpg.Error) database "bh_r2_missing" does not exist (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/21/dbapi)', then 'every check holds', exit 0; GET /api/engines on any database then shows no verdict. conform train --project p: '... could not read project 'p' from its database: DBAPIError ... does not exist ... Start it (pnpm db:up), on the live host with sudo brew services start ...', exit 2.
candidates.cause: core/openferment_core/engine/conform.py:1120-1124 (keep(v) failing is printed with the driver's words and the command returns 0 if v.ok) and conform.py's _unanswered words (a database error read as a server that does not answer)
candidates.evidence: bughunt/notes/R2/scripts/conform_missing_db.sh run from my worktree at 2047f5a (scratch prefix renamed to bh_r2_conform); its output kept in bughunt/notes/R2/conform_missing_db.out: the three blocks and exit codes 2, 0, 2 above.

candidates.title: No test holds the MCP --service relay's 'no proxy' rule: trust_env=True leaves the suite green
candidates.area: mcp_server.Service (the --service relay of D.0, commit 6f85338) and tests/test_mcp_service.py
candidates.statement: Flipping the relay's httpx.Client to trust_env=True keeps test_mcp_service.py green, because its relay tests hand the client a stand-in transport and httpx reads no proxy from the environment once a transport is given; the service's own relay is built with no transport, so with the mutant every relayed tool call, project and assistant name goes through HTTP_PROXY.
candidates.contract: Commit 6f85338: '`--service <origin>` (a loopback address alone, no proxy, no redirect) relays each call to the running service's tool door'; core/openferment_core/mcp_server.py:231-234 'Through no proxy: the call is a loopback one, and a cloud container's HTTPS_PROXY names a proxy elsewhere.'
candidates.reproCommand: python3 bughunt/notes/R2/scripts/mutate.py <worktree of 2047f5a> M16 M17; core/.venv/bin/python bughunt/notes/R2/scripts/proxy_mounts.py
candidates.expected: A test fails when the relay reads the environment's proxy settings, as test_a_redirect_the_service_answers_is_followed_nowhere fails for follow_redirects=True (M17 caught).
candidates.observed: M16 (trust_env=False to True in mcp_server.py:239) survived: test_mcp_service.py passed. proxy_mounts.py: 'MCP --service relay, trust_env=True: HTTPTransport through URL(scheme=b'http', host=b'127.0.0.1', port=8979 ...)' with HTTP_PROXY set and NO_PROXY unset; with trust_env=False the relay keeps its own transport.
candidates.cause: core/tests/test_mcp_service.py (the relay is tested through mcp_server.build(..., transport=<stand-in>), which disables httpx's environment proxies whatever trust_env says); the one served test (test_the_server_started_with_service_writes_through_it_...) runs where NO_PROXY covers loopback or no proxy is set
candidates.evidence: bughunt/notes/R2/mutations.json M16 'survived' (the served-app test deselected, since it binds an ephemeral port outside 8970-8979; in this container NO_PROXY lists 127.0.0.1 and HTTP_PROXY is unset, and CI sets no proxy, so it passes there too by reading); M17 'caught'. bughunt/notes/R2/scripts/proxy_mounts.py output quoted above. The import-url fetch's trust_env (M20, M21) also survives, and proxy_mounts.py shows why it changes nothing there: that client is always handed its pinned transport.
